PRINCIPAL <- 1000

validate_rates <- function(rates) {
  if (!is.numeric(rates) || length(rates) == 0) {
    stop("rates must be a non-empty numeric vector")
  }
  if (anyNA(rates)) {
    stop("rates must not contain missing values")
  }
  invisible(TRUE)
}

invest <- function(rates) {
  validate_rates(rates)
  balance <- PRINCIPAL
  yearly <- numeric(length(rates))
  for (year in seq_along(rates)) {
    growth <- 1 + rates[year] / 100
    balance <- balance * growth
    yearly[year] <- balance
  }
  highest <- max(yearly)
  lowest <- min(yearly)
  profit <- balance - PRINCIPAL
  average <- mean(yearly)
  list(
    final = balance,
    highest = highest,
    lowest = lowest,
    profit = profit,
    average = average
  )
}

money <- function(x) {
  formatted <- formatC(x, format = "f", digits = 2, big.mark = ",")
  paste0("$", formatted)
}

report <- function(rates) {
  result <- invest(rates)
  header <- paste0("Rates (%): ", paste(rates, collapse = ", "))
  text <- c(
    header,
    paste("Years:           ", length(rates)),
    paste("Final balance:   ", money(result$final)),
    paste("Highest balance: ", money(result$highest)),
    paste("Lowest balance:  ", money(result$lowest)),
    paste("Total profit:    ", money(result$profit)),
    paste("Average balance: ", money(result$average))
  )
  cat(text, sep = "\n")
  cat("\n\n")
  invisible(result)
}

main <- function() {
  single <- c(5)
  report(single)
  decade <- c(4.5, 3.2, -1.8, 6.0, 5.5, 2.1, -0.75, 7.25, 3.9, 4.1)
  report(decade)
  volatile <- c(20, -15, 30, -25, 10)
  summary_of_volatile <- report(volatile)
  best_year <- which.max(volatile)
  cat("Best rate in the volatile run:", volatile[best_year],
      "% in year", best_year, "\n")
  cat("Profit per year on average:",
      money(summary_of_volatile$profit / length(volatile)), "\n")
}

main()

Write a function `document(text)` that extracts statistics from a single string representing a paragraph. Split the text into sentences using the period character. split_sentences <- function(text) {
  pieces <- strsplit(text, ".", fixed = TRUE)[[1]]
  trimmed <- trimws(pieces)
  trimmed[nzchar(trimmed)]
}

split_words <- function(sentence) {
  tokens <- strsplit(sentence, " ", fixed = TRUE)[[1]]
  tokens[nzchar(tokens)]
}

strip_punctuation <- function(words) {
  gsub("[^[:alnum:]']", "", words)
}

document <- function(text) {
  if (!is.character(text) || length(text) != 1L) {
    stop("document() expects a single character string")
  }
  sentences <- split_sentences(text)
  words <- unlist(lapply(sentences, split_words), use.names = FALSE)
  cleaned <- strip_punctuation(words)
  cleaned <- cleaned[nzchar(cleaned)]
  sentence_count <- length(sentences)
  word_count <- length(cleaned)
  word_sizes <- nchar(cleaned)
  average <- if (sentence_count > 0L) word_count / sentence_count else 0
  longest <- if (word_count > 0L) max(word_sizes) else 0L
  three_letter <- sum(word_sizes == 3L)
  list(
    sentences = sentence_count,
    words = word_count,
    average_words_per_sentence = average,
    longest_word_length = longest,
    three_letter_words = three_letter
  )
}

format_report <- function(stats) {
  captions <- c(
    "Sentences", "Words", "Average words per sentence",
    "Longest word length", "Three letter words"
  )
  values <- c(
    format(stats$sentences),
    format(stats$words),
    formatC(stats$average_words_per_sentence, format = "f", digits = 2),
    format(stats$longest_word_length),
    format(stats$three_letter_words)
  )
  width <- max(nchar(captions))
  padded <- formatC(captions, width = -width)
  paste0(padded, " : ", values)
}

main <- function() {
  paragraph <- paste(
    "The quick brown fox jumps over the lazy dog.",
    "Programming in R can be very rewarding.",
    "Statistics help us understand text."
  )
  stats <- document(paragraph)
  report <- format_report(stats)
  cat(report, sep = "\n")
  cat("\n")
}

main()

Write polygon(vertices), plus helpers: validation, formatting/report, driver.polygon <- function(vertices) {
  if (!is.list(vertices) || length(vertices) < 3) {
    stop("a polygon needs at least three vertices given as a list")
  }
  lengths_ok <- vapply(vertices, function(v) is.numeric(v) && length(v) == 2, logical(1))
  if (!all(lengths_ok)) {
    stop("each vertex must be a numeric vector of length two")
  }

  xs <- vapply(vertices, function(v) v[1], numeric(1))
  ys <- vapply(vertices, function(v) v[2], numeric(1))

  n <- length(xs)
  nxt <- c(seq_len(n - 1) + 1, 1)
  dx <- xs[nxt] - xs
  dy <- ys[nxt] - ys

  perimeter <- sum(sqrt(dx^2 + dy^2))
  cross <- xs * ys[nxt] - xs[nxt] * ys
  area <- abs(sum(cross)) / 2

  list(
    area = area,
    perimeter = perimeter,
    xmin = min(xs),
    xmax = max(xs),
    ymin = min(ys),
    ymax = max(ys)
  )
}

centroid <- function(vertices) {
  xs <- vapply(vertices, function(v) v[1], numeric(1))
  ys <- vapply(vertices, function(v) v[2], numeric(1))
  c(x = mean(xs), y = mean(ys))
}

format_report <- function(name, props) {
  box <- sprintf(
    "x: [%.3f, %.3f]  y: [%.3f, %.3f]",
    props$xmin, props$xmax, props$ymin, props$ymax
  )
  lines <- c(
    paste0("Shape: ", name),
    sprintf("  area      = %.4f", props$area),
    sprintf("  perimeter = %.4f", props$perimeter),
    paste0("  bounds    = ", box)
  )
  paste(lines, collapse = "\n")
}

regular_ngon <- function(sides, radius) {
  angles <- seq(0, 2 * pi, length.out = sides + 1)[-(sides + 1)]
  lapply(angles, function(a) c(radius * cos(a), radius * sin(a)))
}

main <- function() {
  square <- list(c(0, 0), c(4, 0), c(4, 4), c(0, 4))
  triangle <- list(c(-1, -1), c(3, 0), c(1, 5))
  hexagon <- regular_ngon(6, 2)

  shapes <- list(square = square, triangle = triangle, hexagon = hexagon)
  for (name in names(shapes)) {

    mid <- centroid(shapes[[name]])

}

  if (!is.numeric(delays) || length(delays) == 0) {
    stop("delays must be a non-empty numeric vector of minutes")
  }
  late <- delays[delays > 0]
  late_count <- length(late)
  total_minutes <- sum(late)
  severe_count <- sum(late > 60)
  late_percentage <- 100 * late_count / length(delays)

  if (late_count == 0) {
    max_delay <- NA_real_
    min_delay <- NA_real_
    spread <- NA_real_
    average <- NA_real_
  } else {
    max_delay <- max(late)
    min_delay <- min(late)
    spread <- max_delay - min_delay
    average <- total_minutes / late_count
  }

  list(
    late_count = late_count,
    total_minutes = total_minutes,
    max_delay = max_delay,
    min_delay = min_delay,
    difference = spread,
    average = average,
    severe_count = severe_count,
    late_percentage = late_percentage
  )
}

  if (is.na(value)) {
    return("n/a")

  paste0(formatC(value, format = "f", digits = 1), " min")

  stats <- evaluate(delays)
  header <- paste0("Trains observed: ", length(delays))

    paste0("Total late minutes: ", format_minutes(stats$total_minutes)),

  )
  cat(lines, sep = "\n")
  cat("\n")
  invisible(stats)
}

  if (any(is.na(scores))) {

  shortfall <- 100 - top
  raised <- scores + shortfall
  curved <- pmin(raised, 100)

  lowest <- min(curved)

Tax is eight percent of discounted subtotal. Add discounted subtotal, shipping, and tax for grand total. Calculate effective tax rate by dividing tax by initial subtotal. Determine total amount of discounts and shipping fees combined. Return initial subtotal, discount amount, shipping fee, tax amount, grand total, effective tax rate, and combined fees.

Write a function `solar(generation)` that reviews a numeric vector of daily energy generation. Sum values for total energy. Calculate average daily generation. Identify low sun days generating under ten. Find maximum generation day. Find minimum generation day. Calculate difference between maximum and minimum. Find median daily generation. Estimate monthly generation by multiplying average by thirty. Calculate variance of daily generation. Return total generation, average generation, low sun count, maximum, minimum, difference, median, monthly estimate, and variance.
text_nat:
solar_validate <- function(generation) {
  if (!is.numeric(generation)) {
    stop("generation must be a numeric vector")
  }
  cleaned <- generation[!is.na(generation)]
  if (length(cleaned) == 0) {
    stop("generation must contain at least one non-missing value")
  }
  if (any(cleaned < 0)) {
    stop("generation values cannot be negative")
  }
  cleaned
}

low_sun_days <- function(generation, threshold = 10) {
  generation[generation < threshold]
}

solar <- function(generation) {
  daily <- solar_validate(generation)
  total <- sum(daily)
  average <- mean(daily)
  dim_days <- low_sun_days(daily)
  best <- max(daily)
  worst <- min(daily)
  spread <- best - worst
  middle <- median(daily)
  monthly <- average * 30
  spread_variance <- var(daily)
  list(
    total_generation = total,
    average_generation = average,
    low_sun_count = length(dim_days),
    maximum = best,
    minimum = worst,
    difference = spread,
    median = middle,
    monthly_estimate = monthly,
    variance = spread_variance
  )
}

format_report <- function(report, digits = 2) {
  labels <- c(
    total_generation = "Total generation",
    average_generation = "Average daily generation",
    low_sun_count = "Low sun days (under 10)",
    maximum = "Best day",
    minimum = "Worst day",
    difference = "Best-worst difference",
    median = "Median daily generation",
    monthly_estimate = "Monthly estimate",
    variance = "Variance"
  )
  values <- vapply(report[names(labels)], function(v) {
    formatted <- format(round(v, digits), nsmall = 0)
    trimws(formatted)
  }, character(1))
  paste0(labels, ": ", values)
}

week <- c(14.2, 9.5, 21.8, 3.1, 18.0, 25.4, 7.9, 16.6, 11.3, 22.1)
summary_stats <- solar(week)
cat(format_report(summary_stats), sep = "\n")

overcast <- c(4.5, 8.2, 9.9, 6.0, 12.5)
overcast_stats <- solar(overcast)
cat("\nOvercast stretch\n")
cat(format_report(overcast_stats), sep = "\n")

best_period <- if (summary_stats$average_generation > overcast_stats$average_generation) "sample week" else "overcast stretch"
cat("\nStronger period:", best_period, "\n")

text_es: Write a function `loyalty(purchases)` that processes a numeric vector of purchase amounts. Stars earned is integer floor of each amount. Sum total stars earned. Calculate free drinks by integer division of total stars by twelve. Calculate remaining stars by total stars modulo twelve. Find largest number of stars in a single transaction. Find smallest number of stars in a transaction. Calculate average stars per transaction. Calculate total purchase amount across all transactions. Return total stars, free drinks, remaining stars, largest stars, smallest stars, average stars, and total purchase amount.

Write a function `pack(boxes)` that organizes a numeric vector of box counts per order. Pallet holds fifty boxes. Calculate full pallets needed per order by integer division. Calculate remaining loose boxes per order using modulo. Sum total full pallets. Sum total loose boxes. Count orders requiring at least one full pallet. Find largest single order box count. Find smallest single order box count. Calculate average number of boxes per order. Calculate total boxes processed. Return total full pallets, total loose boxes, large order count, largest order, smallest order, average boxes, and total boxes.

Write a function `loan(principals)` that computes details for a numeric vector of principal amounts. Annual interest rate is five percent, term sixty months. Calculate total interest by principal times rate times five. Calculate total amount to repay by adding interest to principal. Calculate monthly payment by dividing total amount by sixty. Sum monthly payments for total cash flow. Sum interest for total profit. Find highest single monthly payment. Find lowest single monthly payment. Calculate average interest generated per loan. Return total cash flow, total profit, highest payment, lowest payment, average interest, and monthly payments.

`simulate(steps)` takes an integer number of time steps. Start with a prey population of one hundred and a predator population of twenty. Each step, prey grows by a rate of five percent, but loses one percent of its count per predator. Predators grow by zero point five percent per prey, but lose three percent of their own population naturally. Ensure populations do not drop below zero. Track the populations at each step. Return a list containing two lists: the history of prey counts and the history of predator counts.

`hash(message)` takes a string of characters. Convert each character to its ascii integer value. Initialize three accumulators to seven, eleven, and thirteen. For each integer, add it to the first accumulator modulo two hundred fifty six. Multiply the second accumulator by the integer and keep the result modulo two hundred fifty six. Bitwise exclusive or the integer with the third accumulator. Sum the three resulting accumulators together. Return the final sum modulo sixty five thousand five hundred thirty six.

`simulate(accesses)` takes a list of integer page numbers. Maintain a memory holding up to four pages, initially empty, and track the number of page faults. For each access, check if the page is currently in memory. If not, increment the fault count. If memory is full during a fault, remove the page that was accessed furthest in the past. Add the new page and update the access history to mark it as the most recently used. Return the total number of page faults.

`score(shots)` takes a list of distances from the center of a target in centimeters. Initialize a total score and a count of bullseyes to zero. For each shot, award ten points if the distance is under five, eight points if under ten, five points if under twenty, and zero otherwise. Also increment the bullseye count if the distance is strictly under five. Track the longest streak of consecutive bullseyes achieved. Return a list with the total score, total bullseyes, and maximum bullseye streak.

`simulate(usage)` takes a list of integers representing hourly power draw in watts. The battery starts at a maximum capacity of five hundred watt hours. For each hour, subtract the draw from the current capacity. If the capacity drops below twenty percent of the maximum, degrade the maximum capacity by one watt hour permanently. If capacity hits zero, any further draw in that hour is counted as blackout time. Return a list of total blackout hours and the final maximum capacity.

`evaluate(flights)` takes a list of flight distances in miles. Calculate the total miles flown and count the number of individual flights. Determine the base tier as standard. If the total miles exceed twenty five thousand or the flight count exceeds thirty, set the tier to silver. If miles exceed fifty thousand or flights exceed sixty, set the tier to gold. Calculate the additional miles needed to reach the next highest tier based on the current status. Return a list with the achieved tier name and miles to the next tier.

`model(days)` takes an integer number of days to simulate. A plant starts with a height of two centimeters and zero leaves. Each day, the plant grows by ten percent of its current height plus one centimeter. Every time the total height passes a new multiple of ten centimeters, a new leaf grows. If the number of leaves exceeds five, the daily height growth is reduced by twenty percent due to energy diversion. Keep track of the daily heights. Return a list of the final leaf count and the list of heights.

`detect(asteroids)` takes a list of integer sizes representing asteroids moving in a line. Positive sizes move right, negative sizes move left. Initialize an empty stack. For each asteroid, push it to the stack. If a right moving asteroid on the stack is followed by a left moving one, a collision occurs. The smaller asteroid is destroyed. If they are equal in absolute size, both are destroyed. Resolve all collisions before processing the next asteroid. Return a list of the surviving asteroid sizes.

`simulate(crew)` takes the number of crew members aboard. Initialize oxygen reserves to ten thousand units and carbon dioxide filters to one hundred percent health. Each day, every crew member consumes ten units of oxygen and generates twelve units of carbon dioxide. The filters remove the carbon dioxide but lose one percent health for every fifty units processed. If filter health drops below twenty percent, oxygen consumption doubles due to stress. Simulate thirty days. Return a list of the final oxygen reserves and filter health.

Write a function `harvest(plots)` that evaluates a list of triplets containing plot area in acres, rainfall in inches, and fertilizer applied in pounds. Calculate the expected yield for each plot, starting with a base yield of fifty bushels per acre. If rainfall is between twenty and forty inches, multiply the plot's yield by one point two, and if rainfall is below ten inches, multiply by zero point five. For every pound of fertilizer above ten pounds total, add two extra bushels to the plot. Keep a running sum of the overall yield across all plots and count how many plots exceeded one thousand bushels. Return the total yield and the count of highly productive plots. Example: Input [[10, 25, 15], [5, 5, 5]] outputs [610, 125] (Wait, 610 + 125 = 735, count 0). Output is [735, 0].

Write a function `trajectory(initial)` that processes a triplet containing an initial velocity in meters per second, a launch angle in degrees, and a time step in seconds. Convert the launch angle to radians to compute the initial horizontal and vertical velocities. Simulate the flight using a loop that advances time by the given time step. In each step, calculate the new horizontal position, the new vertical position using gravity at nine point eight meters per second squared, and update the maximum height reached. Stop the simulation when the vertical position falls below zero. Return a pair of numbers containing the total horizontal distance traveled and the maximum height achieved. Example: Input [20, 45, 0.1] outputs [40.8, 10.2].

Write a function `fare(trips)` that processes a list of triplets representing distance in miles, duration in minutes, and an indicator for rush hour (one for true, zero for false). Calculate the cost of each trip, starting with a base charge of three dollars. Add two dollars for every mile and fifty cents for every minute. If the trip occurs during rush hour, multiply the entire subtotal by one point five. If the total exceeds fifty dollars, apply a ten percent discount strictly to the portion of the fare above fifty dollars. Accumulate the total revenue for all trips and count how many trips received the large fare discount. Return the total revenue and the discount count. Example: Input [[15, 20, 1], [2, 5, 0]] outputs [72.55, 1].

Write a function `level(events)` that processes a list of pairs where the first element is an event type indicator (zero for monster, one for quest) and the second is experience points gained. A character starts at level one with zero experience, one hundred health, and ten attack power. Iterate through the events and add the experience points. Whenever total experience reaches or exceeds one thousand times the current level, subtract that threshold amount from total experience, increase the level by one, add twenty to health, and add five to attack power. Keep track of how many monsters were defeated and how many quests were completed. Return a list containing the final level, health, attack, remaining experience, monster count, and quest count. Example: Input [[0, 800], [1, 400]] outputs [2, 120, 15, 200, 1, 1].

Write a function `splits(miles)` that takes a list of times in seconds taken to run each consecutive mile of a race. Iterate through the mile times to compute overall statistics. Maintain a running total of the elapsed time and identify the fastest and slowest mile times. Calculate the average pace per mile over the entire run. Check if the sum of the second half of the run is strictly less than the first half, which indicates a negative split. Return the total time, average pace, fastest mile, slowest mile, and a one if a negative split was achieved or zero otherwise. Example: Input [450, 460, 440, 430] outputs [1780, 445, 430, 460, 1].

Write a function `billing(accounts)` that analyzes a list of pairs containing a monthly data allowance in gigabytes and the actual data used in gigabytes. Process each account to determine its monthly bill, where the base plan costs forty dollars. If the actual usage is less than or equal to the allowance, the bill is just the base cost. If the user exceeds the allowance, they are charged fifteen dollars for every full or partial gigabyte over the limit. If an account's usage is strictly less than half of their allowance, they receive a five dollar credit on their bill. Track the total revenue from all bills and the total excess gigabytes consumed across all accounts. Return the revenue and the excess data count. Example: Input [[10, 12.3], [5, 2]] outputs [120, 3].

Write a function `cut(orders)` that takes a standard fabric roll size in yards, followed by a list of requested cut lengths in yards. Simulate cutting the requested lengths from fabric rolls, starting with a fresh roll. For each request, if the length fits on the current roll, subtract it from the remaining length. If the request is larger than the remaining length, the leftover piece is considered waste, and a new roll is started to fulfill the current request. At the end, treat any unused portion of the final roll as waste as well. Maintain a count of total rolls used and accumulate the total yards of wasted fabric. Return a pair with the number of rolls required and the total waste in yards. Example: Input 10 and [4, 5, 3, 6, 2] outputs [3, 10].

Write a function `migration(flocks)` that analyzes a list of flight records, where each record is a triplet containing days in flight, average daily distance in kilometers, and average altitude in meters. Calculate the progress of migrating bird flocks. For each record, find the baseline distance traveled by multiplying days by average daily distance. If the altitude is above two thousand meters, the flock faces high winds, so reduce the calculated distance by ten percent. If the days in flight are strictly greater than ten, subtract a fatigue penalty of fifty kilometers from the distance. Keep a running sum of the adjusted distances for all flocks, and keep track of the maximum adjusted distance achieved by any single flock. Return the total adjusted distance and the maximum individual flock distance. Example: Input [[5, 100, 1500], [12, 80, 2500]] outputs [1314.0, 814.0].

Write a function `demographics(citizens)` that processes a list of pairs representing individuals, where the first element is age in years and the second is an indicator for biological sex (zero for male, one for female). Construct a simplified demographic summary by placing citizens into age brackets: youth for under eighteen, adult for eighteen to sixty four inclusive, and senior for sixty five and over. Count the number of individuals in each age bracket. Simultaneously, maintain a count of males and females within the adult bracket only. Calculate the dependency ratio by adding the youth and senior counts, dividing by the adult count, and multiplying by one hundred. Return a list containing the youth count, adult count, senior count, adult female count, and the dependency ratio. Example: Input [[10, 0], [30, 1], [40, 0], [70, 1]] outputs [1, 2, 1, 1, 100.0].

Write a function `exchange(transactions)` that processes a list of triplets containing an amount in US Dollars, a target currency rate, and a fixed transaction fee in the target currency. For each transaction, multiply the dollar amount by the target exchange rate to get the gross converted amount. Subtract the transaction fee to determine the net amount. If the original dollar amount exceeds one thousand, waive the transaction fee completely. If the final net amount is negative, set it to zero. Sum the net converted amounts to find the total foreign currency generated, and keep a separate count of how many transactions resulted in a net of exactly zero. Return the total net currency and the zero net count. Example: Input [[500, 0.9, 10], [1500, 0.8, 50], [10, 0.5, 10]] outputs [1640.0, 1].

Write a function `buffer(samples)` that evaluates a list of pairs for different chemical solutions, where each pair is the concentration of an acid and the concentration of its conjugate base in moles per liter. Assume the acid has a constant dissociation constant of four point seven six. For each sample, compute the pH using the Henderson Hasselbalch equation, which adds the base ten logarithm of the base divided by the acid to the dissociation constant. A buffer is considered effective if its pH is strictly between three point seven six and five point seven six, and the total concentration of acid plus base is greater than zero point one. Count the number of effective buffers and find the highest pH among all samples. Return the effective count and the maximum pH. Example: Input [[0.1, 0.1], [0.01, 0.01], [0.2, 0.8]] outputs [2, 5.362].

Write a function `hvac(temperatures)` that estimates energy consumption using a list of outside temperatures in Fahrenheit for each hour of the day. The indoor target temperature is set at seventy degrees. For each hour, calculate the absolute difference between the outside temperature and the target. If the difference is five degrees or less, the system remains off and consumes zero energy. If the difference is greater than five, the system consumes zero point five kilowatt hours for every degree of difference. If the outside temperature is strictly above ninety or strictly below thirty, add an extreme weather penalty of two extra kilowatt hours. Accumulate the total daily energy usage and find the single hour with the highest usage. Return both values. Example: Input [72, 60, 95] outputs [19.5, 14.5].

Write a function `toll(vehicles)` that processes a list of triplets for each vehicle passing a toll booth, containing the number of axles, the vehicle weight in tons, and an indicator for electronic toll collection (one for true, zero for false). Calculate the toll fee for each vehicle, starting with a base fee of two dollars. Add one dollar and fifty cents for every axle. If the vehicle weighs strictly more than five tons, add an overweight surcharge of five dollars. If the vehicle uses electronic toll collection, apply a twenty percent discount to the calculated total. Sum the revenue collected from all vehicles. Count how many vehicles were flagged as overweight and how many paid using electronic collection. Return the total revenue, the overweight count, and the electronic count. Example: Input [[2, 3, 1], [4, 6, 0]] outputs [17.0, 1, 1].

Write a function `courier(packages)` that simulates loading delivery vans using a list of package weights in kilograms. Each van has a maximum weight capacity of fifty kilograms. Iterate through the packages in order. If the current package fits in the current van, add its weight to the van. If the package makes the van exceed fifty kilograms, the current van departs, and the current package is placed in a new empty van. Keep a running sum of the empty space left in each departed van. Continue until all packages are loaded, and count the final partially filled van as departed. Return the total number of vans used and the total empty space across all departed vans. Example: Input [20, 25, 30, 10] outputs [2, 15].

Write a function `advertising(episodes)` that processes a list of pairs representing podcast episodes, where each pair contains the number of downloads and the total duration in minutes. Calculate the advertising revenue generated. For each episode, determine the number of ad slots, granting one ad slot for every twenty full minutes of duration. The revenue per slot is calculated as fifty dollars for every one thousand downloads. If an episode has strictly more than fifty thousand downloads, it earns a bonus premium of five hundred dollars per ad slot. Calculate the total revenue across all episodes. Count the total number of ad slots placed and the number of episodes that qualified for the bonus premium. Return the total revenue, ad slot count, and premium episode count. Example: Input [[10000, 45], [60000, 25]] outputs [4500.0, 3, 1].

Write a function `astronomy(coordinates)` that converts equatorial coordinates to galactic coordinates. The input is a list of pairs where each pair contains right ascension and declination in degrees. For each pair, convert the degrees to radians. Calculate the intermediate sine and cosine values for both angles. Apply the standard rotational transformation matrix to align the equatorial plane with the galactic plane. Extract the resulting galactic longitude and galactic latitude in radians, and convert them back to degrees. Return a list of pairs containing the galactic longitude and latitude in degrees. Example input: list containing a pair with right ascension ten and declination twenty.

Write a function `pressure(readings)` to analyze cardiovascular health indicators. The input is a list of pairs, where each pair contains systolic pressure and diastolic pressure. For each pair, calculate the pulse pressure by subtracting the diastolic from the systolic value. Calculate the mean arterial pressure by adding one third of the pulse pressure to the diastolic value. Determine the risk category: if mean arterial pressure is above one hundred and pulse pressure is above sixty, the category is high risk; if mean arterial pressure is below seventy, it is low risk; otherwise, it is normal risk. Return a list of lists containing the pulse pressure, mean arterial pressure, and the category string. Example input: list containing a pair with one hundred twenty and eighty.

Implement a function `fermentation(gravities)` that calculates beer characteristics from gravity readings. The input is a list of pairs representing original gravity and final gravity. For each pair, calculate the apparent attenuation percentage by subtracting the final gravity from the original gravity, dividing by the original gravity minus one, and multiplying by one hundred. Calculate the alcohol by weight by multiplying the gravity drop by seventy six point zero eight. Calculate the alcohol by volume by multiplying the alcohol by weight by the final gravity divided by zero point seven nine four. Calculate the carbohydrate calories per twelve ounces using the final gravity, and the alcohol calories using the alcohol by weight. Return a list of lists containing alcohol by volume, apparent attenuation, and total calories. Example input: list containing a pair with one point zero five zero and one point zero one zero.

Implement a function `exposure(settings)` that computes camera exposure parameters. The input is a list of lists containing aperture f-number, shutter speed in seconds, and film speed rating. For each setting, calculate the base exposure value by taking the base two logarithm of the aperture squared divided by the shutter speed. Calculate the standard exposure value by adjusting the base value for the film speed relative to one hundred. Calculate the scene illuminance in lux using the standard exposure value and a calibration constant of two point five. Calculate the hyperfocal distance for a fifty millimeter lens assuming a circle of confusion of zero point zero three millimeters. Return a list of lists containing the standard exposure value, illuminance in lux, and hyperfocal distance in meters. Example input: list containing two point eight, one hundredth, and four hundred.

Write a function `navigate(points)` that computes great circle distances and bearings. The input is a list of lists where each contains latitude one, longitude one, latitude two, and longitude two in degrees. For each route, convert all four coordinates to radians. Calculate the difference in latitudes and the difference in longitudes. Compute the haversine of the latitude difference and the longitude difference to find the square of half the chord length between the points. Calculate the angular distance in radians using the arc tangent function. Multiply by the earth radius in kilometers to get the distance. Calculate the initial forward bearing in radians using the arc tangent of the sine of the longitude difference and the cosine of the latitudes. Convert the bearing to degrees and normalize it to a compass heading. Return a list of lists containing distance and initial bearing. Example input: list containing thirty, forty, thirty five, and forty five.

Create a function `decay(isotopes)` that simulates the radioactive decay of a parent to a daughter isotope. The input is a list containing the initial parent quantity, parent half life in years, daughter half life in years, and a list of time points in years. Initialize the daughter quantity to zero. Calculate the decay constant for the parent by dividing the natural logarithm of two by its half life. Calculate the decay constant for the daughter similarly. For each time point in the list, calculate the remaining parent quantity using exponential decay. Calculate the accumulated daughter quantity using the Bateman equation, which factors in both the parent decay rate and the daughter decay rate. Return a list of pairs where each pair contains the parent quantity and daughter quantity at that time point. Example input: list containing one thousand, ten, five, and a list of times like zero, five, ten.

Create a function `tides(data)` that estimates water depth between high and low tide. The input is a list of lists containing low tide time in hours from midnight, low tide height in meters, high tide time, high tide height, and a target time in hours. For each tidal cycle, calculate the total duration by subtracting low tide time from high tide time. Calculate the tidal amplitude by subtracting low tide height from high tide height and dividing by two. Calculate the mean water level by adding the amplitude to the low tide height. Calculate the elapsed time from low tide to the target time. Calculate the phase angle for a cosine curve interpolation based on the elapsed time and total duration. Compute the estimated water height at the target time. Return a list of estimated water heights for each cycle. Example input: list containing two, one, eight, five, and five.

Implement a function `spirometry(measurements)` that evaluates lung volumes. The input is a list of lists containing tidal volume, inspiratory reserve volume, expiratory reserve volume, and residual volume in liters. For each patient, calculate the inspiratory capacity by adding tidal volume and inspiratory reserve volume. Calculate the vital capacity by adding the inspiratory capacity to the expiratory reserve volume. Calculate the functional residual capacity by adding the expiratory reserve volume to the residual volume. Calculate the total lung capacity by adding the vital capacity to the residual volume. Calculate the ratio of functional residual capacity to total lung capacity as a percentage. Return a list of lists containing inspiratory capacity, vital capacity, functional residual capacity, total lung capacity, and the capacity ratio. Example input: list containing zero point five, two point five, one point five, and one point two.

Write a function `soil(samples)` that categorizes earth samples based on particle size distribution. The input is a list of lists containing the percentage of sand, silt, and clay. For each sample, extract the three percentages. Calculate a total sum to ensure they add up to one hundred, and if they do not, normalize them by dividing each by the sum. Use logical thresholds to classify the sample: if clay is above forty percent and sand is above forty five percent, classify as sandy clay. If clay is above forty and silt is above forty, classify as silty clay. If clay is above forty, classify as clay. If sand is above eighty five percent, classify as sand. Otherwise, classify as loam. Return a list of strings representing the soil classification for each sample. Example input: list containing fifty, thirty, and twenty.

Create a function `aviation(readings)` that computes critical flight altitudes. The input is a list of lists containing station atmospheric pressure in inches of mercury and ambient temperature in degrees celsius. For each reading, calculate the standard pressure difference by subtracting the station pressure from twenty nine point nine two. Calculate the pressure altitude by multiplying the difference by one thousand and adding field elevation assumed to be zero. Calculate the standard temperature at that pressure altitude by subtracting two degrees for every one thousand feet from fifteen degrees celsius. Calculate the temperature deviation by subtracting the standard temperature from the ambient temperature. Calculate the density altitude by adding the pressure altitude to one hundred twenty times the temperature deviation. Return a list of lists containing pressure altitude and density altitude. Example input: list containing twenty nine point five and twenty five.

Implement a function `inequality(incomes)` that measures wealth distribution. The input is a list of lists containing population fraction and income fraction for various demographic segments, ordered from poorest to richest. Initialize a cumulative population variable to zero and a cumulative income variable to zero. Initialize an area accumulator to zero. For each segment, update the cumulative population by adding the segment population fraction. Update the cumulative income by adding the segment income fraction. Calculate the area of the trapezoid formed under the Lorenz curve for this segment using the previous and current cumulative values. Add this trapezoidal area to the area accumulator. After processing all segments, calculate the Gini coefficient by subtracting twice the total area from one. Return the final Gini coefficient. Example input: list containing lists like zero point two and zero point zero five.

Write a function `acoustics(rooms)` that evaluates sound decay in architectural spaces. The input is a list of lists containing room length, width, height in meters, and an average absorption coefficient. For each room, calculate the floor area by multiplying length and width. Calculate the ceiling area, which is equal to the floor area. Calculate the wall area by multiplying the perimeter by the height. Calculate the total surface area by summing these areas. Calculate the room volume by multiplying length, width, and height. Calculate the equivalent absorption area by multiplying the total surface area by the absorption coefficient. Calculate the Sabine reverberation time by multiplying the volume by zero point one six one and dividing by the equivalent absorption area. Return a list of lists containing room volume, surface area, and Sabine time. Example input: list containing ten, eight, three, and zero point two.

Create a function `queue(systems)` that models waiting line performance. The input is a list of lists containing the customer arrival rate per hour and the server service rate per hour. For each system, calculate the traffic intensity or utilization by dividing the arrival rate by the service rate. validate_property <- function(property) {
  required <- c("area", "age", "bedrooms", "bathrooms")
  absent <- setdiff(required, names(property))
  if (length(absent) > 0) {
    stop(paste("missing property features:", paste(absent, collapse = ", ")))
  }
  values <- unlist(property[required])
  if (!is.numeric(values) || any(is.na(values))) {
    stop("all property features must be numeric and non-missing")
  }
  if (any(values < 0)) {
    stop("property features cannot be negative")
  }
  invisible(TRUE)
}

appraise <- function(property) {
  validate_property(property)
  area <- property$area
  age <- property$age
  bedrooms <- property$bedrooms
  bathrooms <- property$bathrooms

  base_value <- area * 150
  depreciated <- base_value - age * 2000
  bedroom_bonus <- bedrooms * 10000
  bathroom_bonus <- bathrooms * 15000
  subtotal <- depreciated + bedroom_bonus + bathroom_bonus
  subtotal * 1.05
}

appraisal_breakdown <- function(property) {
  validate_property(property)
  base_value <- property$area * 150
  age_adjustment <- -property$age * 2000
  bedroom_bonus <- property$bedrooms * 10000
  bathroom_bonus <- property$bathrooms * 15000
  subtotal <- base_value + age_adjustment + bedroom_bonus + bathroom_bonus
  final_value <- appraise(property)
  list(
    base_value = base_value,
    age_adjustment = age_adjustment,
    bedroom_bonus = bedroom_bonus,
    bathroom_bonus = bathroom_bonus,
    subtotal = subtotal,
    location_premium = final_value - subtotal,
    appraised_value = final_value
  )
}

format_currency <- function(amount) {
  prefix <- if (amount < 0) "-$" else "$"
  paste0(prefix, formatC(abs(amount), format = "f", digits = 2, big.mark = ","))
}

report <- function(label, property) {
  parts <- appraisal_breakdown(property)
  lines <- paste0(
    "  ", format(names(parts), width = 18), " ",
    vapply(parts, format_currency, character(1))
  )
  header <- sprintf("%s (%g sqft, %g yrs, %gbd/%gba)",
                    label, property$area, property$age,
                    property$bedrooms, property$bathrooms)
  cat(header, lines, sep = "\n")
  cat("\n")
  invisible(parts$appraised_value)
}

main <- function() {
  starter_home <- list(area = 1200, age = 25, bedrooms = 3, bathrooms = 1)
  family_home <- list(area = 2400, age = 8, bedrooms = 4, bathrooms = 3)
  new_build <- list(area = 1800, age = 0, bedrooms = 3, bathrooms = 2)
  portfolio <- list(Starter = starter_home, Family = family_home, New = new_build)

  totals <- vapply(names(portfolio),
                   function(nm) report(nm, portfolio[[nm]]),
                   numeric(1))
  cat("Portfolio total:", format_currency(sum(totals)), "\n")
}

The entry point is `fleet(route)` where the parameter is a list containing total distance, number of stops, and vehicle miles per gallon. Extract the total distance, number of stops, and vehicle miles per gallon. Calculate the fuel needed by dividing distance by the miles per gallon. Calculate the fuel cost by multiplying the fuel needed by three point five. Calculate the driver wage by assuming a steady speed of fifty miles per hour and a rate of twenty dollars per hour. Extract the wind speed, blade radius, and efficiency factor. Calculate the swept area using pi times the radius squared. Calculate the kinetic energy flux using the swept area, a standard air density of one point two, and the cube of the wind speed. Multiply the flux by the Betz limit of zero point five nine to find the maximum theoretical power. Multiply this theoretical power by the given efficiency. Calculate the shrinkage percentage by dividing the missing items by the expected inventory. Calculate the total financial loss by multiplying the missing items by the unit value. For each routine, multiply the judge score by the difficulty rating to get the base score, calculate the penalty by multiplying the deduction by zero point five, and subtract the penalty from the base score to get the final score. For each orchard section, calculate the base yield by multiplying the number of trees by fifty, and if the age is greater than eight, add twenty apples per tree to the base yield. Calculate the frost penalty by multiplying the frost days by zero point zero five, reduce the base yield by this percentage to get the actual yield, and find the lost apples by subtracting the actual yield from the base yield. Create a function `aerodynamics(speeds, densities, areas)` to calculate forces on vehicle models. Initialize a total drag accumulator, a total lift accumulator, and an empty list of net forces before looping through the wind speeds, air densities, and frontal areas. Calculate the dynamic pressure by multiplying zero point five by the density and by the square of the wind speed. Calculate the drag force by multiplying the dynamic pressure, the area, and a drag coefficient of zero point three, and calculate the lift force by multiplying the same dynamic pressure and area by a lift coefficient of zero point one five. Add the drag force to the total drag, add the lift force to the total lift, calculate the net force by subtracting the lift from the drag, and append it to the net forces list. Return the total drag, total lift, and the list of net forces. Example: Given [10], [1.2], and [2], it returns [36, 18, [18]].

aerodynamics <- function(speeds, densities, areas) {
  drag_coefficient <- 0.3
  lift_coefficient <- 0.15
  total_drag <- 0
  total_lift <- 0
  net_forces <- list()

  for (i in seq_along(speeds)) {
    speed <- speeds[i]
    air_density <- densities[i]
    area <- areas[i]
    dynamic_pressure <- 0.5 * air_density * speed^2
    drag_force <- dynamic_pressure * area * drag_coefficient
    lift_force <- dynamic_pressure * area * lift_coefficient
    total_drag <- total_drag + drag_force
    total_lift <- total_lift + lift_force
    net_force <- drag_force - lift_force
    net_forces[[length(net_forces) + 1]] <- net_force
  }

  list(total_drag, total_lift, net_forces)
}

validate_inputs <- function(speeds, densities, areas) {
  sizes <- c(length(speeds), length(densities), length(areas))
  if (length(unique(sizes)) != 1) {
    stop("speeds, densities and areas must have the same length")
  }
  if (any(speeds < 0) || any(densities <= 0) || any(areas <= 0)) {
    stop("speeds must be non-negative and densities/areas positive")
  }
  invisible(TRUE)
}

format_report <- function(result) {
  total_drag <- result[[1]]
  total_lift <- result[[2]]
  net_forces <- unlist(result[[3]])
  model_lines <- sprintf("model %d: net force = %.2f N", seq_along(net_forces), net_forces)
  summary_line <- sprintf("total drag = %.2f N, total lift = %.2f N", total_drag, total_lift)
  paste(c(model_lines, summary_line), collapse = "\n")
}

main <- function() {
  single_speed <- c(10)
  single_density <- c(1.2)
  single_area <- c(2)
  validate_inputs(single_speed, single_density, single_area)
  single_result <- aerodynamics(single_speed, single_density, single_area)
  cat(format_report(single_result), "\n\n")

  fleet_speeds <- c(15, 22.5, 30, 40)
  fleet_densities <- c(1.225, 1.2, 1.18, 1.1)
  fleet_areas <- c(1.8, 2.0, 2.2, 2.4)
  validate_inputs(fleet_speeds, fleet_densities, fleet_areas)
  fleet_result <- aerodynamics(fleet_speeds, fleet_densities, fleet_areas)
  cat(format_report(fleet_result), "\n\n")

  net_values <- unlist(fleet_result[[3]])
  best_index <- which.max(net_values)
  cat(sprintf("highest net force: model %d at %.2f N\n", best_index, net_values[best_index]))
}

main()

trajectory <- function(velocities, angles, winds) {
  n <- length(velocities)
  if (length(angles) != n || length(winds) != n) {
    stop("velocities, angles and winds must all have the same length")
  }
  total_time <- 0
  max_distance <- 0
  distances <- list()
  for (i in seq_len(n)) {
    angle_rad <- angles[i] * 0.017
    vertical <- velocities[i] * sin(angle_rad)
    horizontal <- velocities[i] * cos(angle_rad)
    flight_time <- vertical / 5
    base_distance <- horizontal * flight_time
    adjusted <- base_distance - winds[i] * flight_time
    total_time <- total_time + flight_time
    distances[[length(distances) + 1]] <- adjusted
    if (adjusted > max_distance) {
      max_distance <- adjusted
    }
  }
  list(max_distance, total_time, distances)
}

summarise_shots <- function(result) {
  distances <- unlist(result[[3]])
  mean_distance <- if (length(distances) > 0) mean(distances) else 0
  spread <- if (length(distances) > 0) max(distances) - min(distances) else 0
  list(count = length(distances), mean = mean_distance, spread = spread)
}

format_report <- function(velocities, angles, winds, result) {
  distances <- unlist(result[[3]])
  header <- sprintf("%10s %8s %8s %12s", "velocity", "angle", "wind", "distance")
  lines <- character(length(distances))
  for (i in seq_along(distances)) {
    lines[i] <- sprintf("%10.1f %8.1f %8.1f %12.2f",
                        velocities[i], angles[i], winds[i], distances[i])
  }
  stats <- summarise_shots(result)
  footer <- c(
    sprintf("shots:         %d", stats$count),
    sprintf("max distance:  %.2f", result[[1]]),
    sprintf("total time:    %.2f", result[[2]]),
    sprintf("mean distance: %.2f", stats$mean),
    sprintf("spread:        %.2f", stats$spread)
  )
  paste(c(header, lines, "", footer), collapse = "\n")
}

main <- function() {
  single <- trajectory(c(100), c(30), c(5))
  cat(format_report(c(100), c(30), c(5), single), "\n\n")

  velocities <- c(80, 100, 120, 150)
  angles <- c(25, 30, 45, 60)
  winds <- c(0, 5, 10, -3)
  volley <- trajectory(velocities, angles, winds)
  cat(format_report(velocities, angles, winds, volley), "\n")

  best_index <- which.max(unlist(volley[[3]]))
  cat(sprintf("\nbest shot: %.0f m/s at %.0f degrees with wind %.0f\n",
              velocities[best_index], angles[best_index], winds[best_index]))
}

main()

The engine has a specific impulse of three hundred twenty seconds and a thrust of four hundred fifty kilonewtons. First, determine the exhaust velocity by multiplying specific impulse by the standard gravity of nine point eight one. Initialize the total velocity change to zero and the current total mass to the dry mass plus twenty thousand kilograms of fuel. For each burn duration in the list, compute the mass of fuel consumed by dividing thrust by exhaust velocity, then multiplying by the duration. Update the current mass by subtracting the consumed fuel. Next, compute the mass ratio as the previous mass divided by the new mass, and find the velocity change for that step by multiplying exhaust velocity by the natural logarithm of the mass ratio. Accumulate this velocity change. If the current mass drops below the dry mass, stop the sequence immediately. Return a list containing the final mass and the total accumulated velocity change. Next, calculate the salinity contribution by multiplying salinity by zero point eight and adding it to the pure water density to establish the base density. Compute the secant bulk modulus base by taking nineteen thousand six hundred fifty two plus temperature multiplied by one hundred forty eight minus squared temperature multiplied by two. Adjust the bulk modulus for salinity by adding fifty four times the salinity. Further adjust for pressure by adding three point two times the pressure. First, convert the mean anomaly to radians. Compute the eccentric anomaly by iterating five times: start with the eccentric anomaly equal to the mean anomaly, and repeatedly subtract the difference between the eccentric anomaly minus eccentricity times the sine of the eccentric anomaly minus the mean anomaly, all divided by one minus eccentricity times the cosine of the eccentric anomaly. First, isolate the target values for each of the three elements from the list. Compute the required concentration addition for nitrogen by multiplying its target by one point one to account for absorption inefficiencies. Compute the volume of nitrogen solution needed by dividing the adjusted target by fifty, then multiplying by the reservoir volume. Repeat this for phosphorus: multiply the target by one point two for inefficiency, divide by thirty, and multiply by the reservoir volume. For potassium, multiply the target by one point zero five, divide by forty, and multiply by the reservoir volume. Calculate the total volume of all dosed liquids. Compute the final expected electrical conductivity increase by multiplying the total dosed volume by zero point zero zero two. Return a list containing the three individual dosages, the total volume, and the conductivity increase. Example: given targets of one hundred, fifty, and one hundred twenty, and a volume of two hundred, return the calculated dosage schedule.

dose <- function(targets, volume) {
  if (length(targets) != 3L) {
    stop("targets must contain three values: nitrogen, phosphorus, potassium")
  }
  if (!is.numeric(volume) || length(volume) != 1L || volume <= 0) {
    stop("volume must be a single positive number of liters")
  }

  nitrogen_target <- as.numeric(targets[[1]])
  phosphorus_target <- as.numeric(targets[[2]])
  potassium_target <- as.numeric(targets[[3]])

  nitrogen_adjusted <- nitrogen_target * 1.1
  nitrogen_ml <- nitrogen_adjusted / 50 * volume

  phosphorus_adjusted <- phosphorus_target * 1.2
  phosphorus_ml <- phosphorus_adjusted / 30 * volume

  potassium_adjusted <- potassium_target * 1.05
  potassium_ml <- potassium_adjusted / 40 * volume

  total_ml <- nitrogen_ml + phosphorus_ml + potassium_ml
  ec_increase <- total_ml * 0.002

  list(
    nitrogen = nitrogen_ml,
    phosphorus = phosphorus_ml,
    potassium = potassium_ml,
    total = total_ml,
    ec_increase = ec_increase
  )
}

format_schedule <- function(schedule, volume) {
  header <- sprintf("Dosing schedule for a %.1f L reservoir", volume)
  lines <- c(
    header,
    strrep("-", nchar(header)),
    sprintf("Nitrogen solution  : %8.2f mL", schedule$nitrogen),
    sprintf("Phosphorus solution: %8.2f mL", schedule$phosphorus),
    sprintf("Potassium solution : %8.2f mL", schedule$potassium),
    sprintf("Total liquid added : %8.2f mL", schedule$total),
    sprintf("Expected EC rise   : %8.3f mS/cm", schedule$ec_increase)
  )
  paste(lines, collapse = "\n")
}

report <- function(targets, volume) {
  schedule <- dose(targets, volume)
  concentrate_share <- schedule$total / (volume * 1000) * 100
  text <- format_schedule(schedule, volume)
  cat(text, "\n", sep = "")
  cat(sprintf("Concentrates make up %.3f%% of the reservoir volume\n",
              concentrate_share))
  invisible(schedule)
}

main <- function() {
  npk_targets <- list(100, 50, 120)
  reservoir_volume <- 200
  schedule <- report(npk_targets, reservoir_volume)

  top_up_volume <- 75
  cat("\n")
  report(npk_targets, top_up_volume)

  cumulative_ec <- schedule$ec_increase + dose(npk_targets, top_up_volume)$ec_increase
  cat(sprintf("\nCombined EC rise across both doses: %.3f mS/cm\n", cumulative_ec))
}

main()
